keyChanges.title: Austin cameras log Cybercabs outside the paid geofence
keyChanges.description: Tesla North on Nov. 2 cited Robotaxi Tracker cameras outside the Austin boundary mapped as of Oct. 23. On 32 southwest cameras, 21 recorded at least one Cybercab. Weekly detections rose from 1 in the week of Sep. 28 to 9, then 23, then 33 in the week of Oct. 26–Nov. 1. North of the fence, detections the tracker labels engineering rose from none in early October to 27 in the latest week, around Anderson Mill, Parmer, Lakeline, and Highway 620. Those figures are camera events. Tesla has not confirmed a paid-service expansion past the published geofence.

positive_signals: Southwest cameras outside the Oct. 23 Austin boundary logged Cybercab detections rising to 33 in the week of Oct. 26–Nov. 1
North-of-fence detections labeled engineering rose to 27 in the latest week along Anderson Mill, Parmer, Lakeline, and Highway 620
negative_signals: 33 and 27 are camera events, and 21 of 32 southwest cameras simply saw at least one Cybercab
Tesla has not confirmed paid service outside the published Austin geofence
The counts are not a distinct-vehicle floor and do not change the Austin dispatch census

keyChanges.title: Fort Worth Robotaxi opens Nov 2 on Model Y; Cybercab stays Austin-only
keyChanges.description: Tesla's Robotaxi account set Fort Worth service to start Monday, Nov. 2, 2026, at 6 a.m. CT, the fourth Texas city after Austin, Dallas, and Houston. The posted map covers downtown and runs north toward Saginaw, west past White Settlement, southwest toward Benbrook, and east near Haltom City and Forest Hill. Not a Tesla App measured about 143 square miles and called the service unsupervised. robotaxistats later measured about 145 square miles, water included, and also lists unsupervised Model Y. Tesla North reports that Tesla did not state a vehicle count, a safety-monitor status, a price, whether the free-first-ride offer applies, or whether the zone connects to Dallas. The cars in Fort Worth are Model Y. Paid Cybercab service is still Austin-only. Teslarati's Nov. 7 app write-up says riders in Dallas, Houston, Fort Worth, and Florida are still matched to Model Y, so the Q3-call line that Cybercab would reach Dallas in November was still unmet at the end of this window.

positive_signals: Official Robotaxi account set a Monday Nov. 2, 6 a.m. CT start
Fourth Texas city and the first new Robotaxi city in about three months
Not a Tesla App and robotaxistats both classify the launch as unsupervised Model Y service
Downtown geofence traced at roughly 143–145 square miles toward Saginaw, White Settlement, Benbrook, Haltom City, and Forest Hill
negative_signals: Tesla did not disclose a vehicle count, fare, monitor status, or a link to the Dallas zone
Fort Worth service is Model Y; paid Cybercab rides remain Austin-only
Dallas Cybercab, described as coming this month, was still unmet on Nov. 7
The 143 and 145 square-mile figures are third-party map traces, and neither is a fleet count

keyChanges.title: NHTSA Question 8 Cybercab compliance answers stay fully withheld
keyChanges.description: Tesla North reported on Nov. 3 that Tesla answered NHTSA special order AQ26002 by the Oct. 30 deadline. The public file for Question 8, how Cybercab complies with each applicable FMVSS, is a one-page placeholder created Oct. 30, 2026. It states that the remaining responsive documents have a Confidential Business Information request from the manufacturer for the entirety of each document. NHTSA has not granted or denied that request and has not published a violation finding. The same public record still omits Tesla's answers on temporary driver controls, which standards it says do not apply, the foot-brake rule without a pedal, and any Part 555 exemption. Commercial Cybercab service in Austin is already running while the compliance method stays off the public record. This is the FMVSS certification special order, separate from a crash investigation.

positive_signals: Tesla met the Oct. 30 special-order deadline
NHTSA has not published a violation finding; the file shows a CBI request rather than a missing response
negative_signals: Every document responsive to Question 8 is withheld in full under a manufacturer CBI request
The public record is a one-page placeholder created Oct. 30, 2026; confidentiality is neither granted nor denied
Temporary driver controls, inapplicable-standards claims, the foot-brake rule without a pedal, and any Part 555 exemption are still unpublished
Austin commercial Cybercab service is operating while the FMVSS compliance method is secret

keyChanges.title: Robotaxi app 26.11.0 compares Cybercab and Model Y, mostly in Austin
keyChanges.description: Teslarati reported on Nov. 7 that Robotaxi app version 26.11.0 shows ETA, wait, availability, and fare for Cybercab and Model Y on one screen. The screen comes from a rider video, and Tesla has not posted release notes. The comparison is concentrated in Austin. The same article says Dallas, Houston, Fort Worth, and Florida riders are still matched with Model Y. A figure of 1,576 Cybercab sightings in Austin on Halloween is a camera-event total. The article still quotes the older 1,204-vehicle Texas roster.

positive_signals: App 26.11.0 surfaces ETA, wait, availability, and fare for Cybercab versus Model Y on one screen
Austin riders can see both vehicle types before a match
negative_signals: No official Tesla release notes; the screen was shown in a rider video
Dallas, Houston, Fort Worth, and Florida riders are still matched only to Model Y
1,576 Halloween Cybercab sightings are camera events, and the article still cites the older 1,204 roster

keyChanges.title: RDW Caps Europe Speed Margin at 10% and Locks In the Assisted-Driving Name
keyChanges.description: On 3 November 2026 the Dutch vehicle authority RDW said it had assessed changes Tesla asked it to review and folded them into the existing FSD Supervised type approval. The name on the in-car display, in the manual, and in other driver information becomes Tesla Assisted Driving (TAD) for vehicles with hardware 4.0 or later. The driver-set speed margin, which could be set at +50% over the posted limit, is now capped at +10%. It resets to 0% every time the car starts, and other speed-related functions are disabled by default. RDW said it found no adverse or unintended effects and that the existing approval stays valid on the same conditions and for the same use, so it does not need to be amended or extended. RDW notified the nine other member states that already accept that approval: Belgium, Croatia, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Slovakia, and Slovenia. That is still ten countries, not a new one. The EU Technical Committee on Motor Vehicles process remains underway, and RDW said those talks are confidential and it will not discuss them. Teslarati reports that the cap and rename line up with conditions German authorities had already set; they are not a new bloc vote. A +10% margin still lets the system drive over the limit. The driver stays responsible. The United Kingdom is not on the notified list.

positive_signals: RDW formally approved the changes on 3 November 2026 and said its check found no adverse or unintended effects on system behavior
Maximum speed margin cut from +50% to +10%, with the setting reset to 0% at every start and other speed functions off by default
Tesla Assisted Driving is now the name in the approval's driver-facing materials for HW4 and later
The nine other states that recognize the Dutch approval were notified
negative_signals: RDW did not amend or extend the type approval; it called the package minor changes the manufacturer requested
The system was type-approved while a driver could set it 50% over the posted limit, including in urban zones
A 10% margin still permits speeding; it does not meet a zero-over-limit standard
The EU-wide TCMV decision is still pending and confidential. No new country was added, and the UK is outside this notice
The rename does not change the function. It remains supervised driver assistance, and the driver remains responsible

keyChanges.title: Korean Consumer Group Files KFTC Complaint Over FSD Sold on Ineligible Cars
keyChanges.description: On 5 November 2026 the Citizens' Council for Consumer Sovereignty said it had reported Tesla Korea to the Korea Fair Trade Commission for allegedly violating the Display and Advertising Act and the E-Commerce Act. The group says buyers were not clearly told, before paying, whether their specific car could use Full Self-Driving. Chosun, citing Tesla figures given to the National Assembly as of 6 October, said only 54,303 of 227,902 registered Teslas (23.8%) were FSD-compatible, so 76.2% were not. TeslaNorth, citing a Reuters review of the draft complaint, reported that about 99% of 2025 new Teslas could not legally run FSD, that the lump-sum option was still offered at 9.043 million won (about US$6,726), and that the group wants a temporary stop to marketing on ineligible cars, administrative fines, and a referral to investigators. US-built cars can use FSD under the Korea-US free trade agreement. Shanghai-built Model 3 and Model Y cars do not, and need a separate approval. Order-screen warnings about supervision and regulatory limits were, the group says, too generic to show whether a given car was eligible. Tesla had not commented to Reuters as of 4 November. This is a filing, not a KFTC finding. An earlier Seoul court dismissal of refund claims and an unresolved 22 October exemption request to the transport ministry are prior events, not a certification.

positive_signals: US-built Teslas can already use FSD in Korea under the Korea-US FTA recognition of American safety standards

The 29 October Seoul Central District Court dismissal of an 89-owner refund suit held that the contracts were not a promise of driverless automation and that regulatory delay was not itself a breach. That is a civil result, not an advertising clearance
negative_signals: A consumer group filed with the KFTC on 5 November alleging advertising and e-commerce violations for selling FSD on cars that cannot legally use it

Assembly data cited by Chosun: only 23.8% of registered Korean Teslas were FSD-compatible as of 6 October. Reuters-reported draft figures put about 99% of 2025 new Teslas outside legal use, against 183,407 China-built cars that cannot run it
Buyers of China-made Model 3 and Model Y could still purchase the 9.043 million won option in March 2026
The draft complaint seeks a marketing halt, fines, and a referral to investigators. Tesla had not answered Reuters
Shanghai-built cars remain uncertified for FSD. A KFTC complaint is not an approval, and no finding has been issued

keyChanges.title: Supervised miles pass 17 billion, about 300 million above late October
keyChanges.description: Tesla's live FSD (Supervised) safety page showed more than 17.003 billion miles and more than 6.757 billion city miles on November 2, across 17 markets. Tesla North places that just above the roughly 16.7 billion miles on the same page around October 27. The counter advances at the fleet's average miles per second, so this is a round-number crossing rather than a new census. The feature still requires an attentive driver. Unsupervised miles are tracked on a separate Robotaxi report. The article's note that more than 75% of new North American deliveries took FSD in the third quarter is a prior-quarter attach rate, not a November software change. Customer cars are still on supervised v14, and v15 is not in this print.

sentiment.headline: positive
sentiment.rationale: A round number on a supervised, rate-based counter is not a capability step. The gain versus late October is about 300 million miles.

positive_signals: Tesla's safety page showed more than 17.003 billion supervised miles and more than 6.757 billion city miles on November 2
The print is above the roughly 16.7 billion miles Tesla North cites for the same page around October 27, so the logged dataset did grow
negative_signals: The product is still FSD (Supervised); an attentive driver is still required
The gain is about 300 million miles, and the page increments at an average fleet rate rather than a fresh audit
v15 is not part of this counter, and unsupervised miles sit on a separate Robotaxi report
The 75% North American attach line in the writeup is a third-quarter figure, not a November software change

key_metrics.actual: 17.003 billion supervised miles; 6.757 billion city miles
key_metrics.target: Customer v15 still unshipped; unsupervised miles are a separate report
key_metrics.trajectory: About 300 million miles above the late-October print

keyChanges.title: 2026.38.5.12 keeps the same supervised v14.3.13 notes
keyChanges.description: Not a Tesla App lists firmware 2026.38.5.12, dated November 4, as FSD (Supervised) v14.3.13 on HW4 and v14.3 Lite on HW3, and says it is an updated build of v14.3.13 whose release notes are unchanged. The notes are still the supervised v14.3.13 list (reinforcement-learning stage, vision encoder, MLIR runtime, parking, emergency vehicles, small animals) with the same unshipped items: reasoning beyond destination handling, and pothole avoidance. Basenor, citing Teslascope, called a November 5 push of about 1,650 additional AI4 cars a third wave and an FSD bump. It is not a new version. Customer software remains supervised v14, HW3 stays on the distilled Lite build, and v15 is still absent from a customer OTA. Basenor's wave note tells HW3 owners this push does not include the FSD package, so the Lite side is not clearly moving with the AI4 wave. TeslaFi showed about 1,450 cars and 11.8% of its sample on this specific build. That is a tracker share of one point release, not a fleet census. A week earlier, 2026.38.5.11 already carried these identical notes.

positive_signals: Not a Tesla App shows 2026.38.5.12 actually installing, about 1,450 TeslaFi cars and 11.8% of that sample, with a November 5 Teslascope wave of roughly 1,650 more AI4 vehicles
The build does not roll back the v14.3.13 training and vision claims already in the notes
negative_signals: Release notes are unchanged from v14.3.13. No new driving behavior versus 2026.38.5.11
Customer cars remain on supervised v14. v15 is not in this OTA
HW3 is still v14.3 Lite. Basenor describes the November 5 wave as AI4-only
Notes still list reasoning beyond destination handling and pothole avoidance as upcoming, not shipped

key_metrics.target: Customer v15, still unshipped; unsupervised guidance remains around Q2 2027
key_metrics.trajectory: Point builds of the same supervised notes, not a version step

keyChanges.title: Published robot-hand patent is a 2022 design, not a production hand
keyChanges.description: On November 5 the USPTO published Tesla application US 2026/0346473 A1, "Underactuated hand with cable-driven fingers." TeslaNorth and Drive Tesla Canada both describe one floating tendon-like cable per finger: a thickened tip sits loose until a pull catches a ledge and curls two hinged sections, with return springs and Hall sensors. The U.S. filing is the March 20, 2025 national-stage entry of a PCT filed October 2, 2023, with priority to September 30, 2022 provisionals. Drawings show a humanoid. The text does not name Optimus. TeslaNorth says this is an earlier, simpler architecture than the higher-degree-of-freedom forearm-driven hand patents published in April 2026. Drive Tesla Canada reports an examiner pushed back on the claims as written on October 27, 2026. There is no grip strength, no cable life, and no statement that this finger is on the bots Tesla calls production-quality. A four-year-old underactuated sketch does not show the production hand is solved.

positive_signals: The application is a real USPTO publication, not a rumor, and it tries to drive two joints with one cable
Fewer actuators per finger is the parts-count problem Musk has named as the barrier to volume hands
negative_signals: It is an application, not a grant, and Drive Tesla Canada says the examiner already objected to the claims on October 27
Priority is September 2022, and TeslaNorth says the design is older and simpler than hand patents published in April 2026
Optimus is not named, and there is no grip, durability, or yield figure tying the cable to Fremont output

keyChanges.title: Musk says Tesla will probably rent Optimus, with no price
keyChanges.description: At the 33rd Annual Baron Investment Conference on November 6, Ron Baron asked whether Tesla would rent or sell Optimus. Musk answered, "I think probably rent them." Not a Tesla App, working from the same clip Drive Tesla Canada covered, reports he said the robot should at first cost about as much as a car to build and then much less, and that he accepted a path from about $30,000 down toward $20,000. He named no rental rate, term, or start date. Drive Tesla notes the exchange was brief and is not a finished business model. The "five times a human" line is a projection from a robot working on the order of 168 hours a week versus a 40-hour person, not measured output. The remarks do not move external supply off the end of 2027, do not undo last week's denial of December orders, and do not say how many Fremont bots have actually been finished. Headlines that Tesla "will rent" a robot that "costs $20-30K" turn a "probably" and a build-cost remark into a product offer.

positive_signals: The rent-versus-sell line was said on stage at the Baron conference, not planted by an unnamed source
A build cost that falls from about $30,000 toward $20,000, if it arrives, is the first time this week Musk tied a number to Optimus cost rather than a customer sticker
negative_signals: "Probably" is not a rental program: no price, term, volume, or start date
The $20,000-$30,000 band is a build-cost glide path Musk accepted in the interview, not a price a customer can pay, and it sits on top of the old consumer sticker
Five-times productivity is hours arithmetic, not a factory result
Outside deliveries remain an end-of-2027 hope, December orders were already denied, and Fremont still has no disclosed unit count

keyChanges.title: Tesla slide sets SI6 at 80x SI4 and leaves Dojo D3 undated
keyChanges.description: A product slide titled "The chips powering our products" was photographed and posted on Nov 4, then written up by Tom's Hardware on Nov 6. It relabels the inference line SI4, SI5, and SI6 and the training part D3. On the slide, SI5 is 3nm/2nm, a multi-chip module, a 40x gain versus SI4 from "8x compute x 5x silicon optimization," and 6x the memory. SI6 is 2nm, a multi-chip module, an 80x gain, and 9x the memory. D3's node is marked TBA. The only architecture line is a chiplet using 2.5D and 3D stacked HBM, "optimized for space, training, and scaling." That is a real break from the cancelled SRAM wafer-scale Dojo, and it is also an admission that the replacement has no process and no date. Tom's Hardware's comparison table adds status labels such as nearing production, 96GB and 144GB capacities, 250-800W, and a 2029-2030 SI6 window. Those figures are not on the slide. The 96GB and 144GB figures match last month's already-filed LPDDR cut, not a new increase. The slide calls current SI4 a 5nm FCBGA part; Tom's says that label is wrong and the chip is Samsung 7nm-class, so the deck is not a reliable process document. Teslarati, Tesla North, and Not a Tesla App carried no tape-out, yield, or shipment this week. Near-term supply is unchanged: Taylor is still trial, 2nm volume is still a 2027 event, and the prior call still has AI5 in Optimus around April 2027 with no car date.

positive_signals: The Nov 4 slide states SI5 at 40x SI4 on a 3nm/2nm multi-chip module with 6x memory, and SI6 at 80x with 9x memory on a 2nm multi-chip module.
D3 is drawn as a chiplet with 2.5D and 3D stacked HBM, a concrete break from the cancelled SRAM wafer-scale Dojo.
negative_signals: D3's node is TBA, with no performance figure and no schedule. SI6 has no year on the slide. The 2029-2030 window is Tom's Hardware inferring from Samsung's roadmap, not a Tesla date.
The 40x claim and the 6x/9x memory multiples match prior Musk targets and last month's RAM cut to 96GB on AI5 and 144GB on AI6. The slide does not move Taylor past trial or put AI5 in a car.
The same slide calls today's SI4 a 5nm part. Tom's Hardware says that is wrong and the shipping chip is Samsung 7nm-class.
No foundry, wafer count, or yield is named for SI6 or D3, and Intel 14A is not on the slide. Tier-1 Tesla outlets did not confirm the deck.

keyChanges.title: Digitimes says TSMC would run Terafab; the companies have not confirmed
keyChanges.description: On Nov. 2, Digitimes reported that unnamed supply-chain sources say Musk is preparing to reopen talks in which TSMC would take primary responsibility for Terafab construction and operations, with equity and investment still unsettled. Benzinga, citing that report, said Tesla, SpaceX, and TSMC did not comment. The claim reverses Musk's October line that his companies would build and run the fab and that TSMC would at most sublease space. His Nov. 6 Baron remarks still describe his own Austin research fab and a Grimes County production site. He did not hand operations to TSMC. No agreement, permit change, or tool move was announced. The body of the Digitimes piece is behind a paywall; the lede and the Benzinga write-up are the public record.

positive_signals: A foundry that already runs leading-edge lines is again in the conversation, which is the realistic path to commissioning on the stated timeline
Digitimes is a Taiwan semiconductor trade paper, not a single blog rewrite
negative_signals: Tesla, SpaceX, and TSMC did not confirm the talks
Musk's public October position was that TSMC would not run Terafab
Six days later he still described his companies iterating in Austin and scaling in Grimes County
Anonymous sourcing, no term sheet, and no change on the construction site
Needing TSMC to build and run the fab would mean the in-house plan has stalled before a single chip

keyChanges.title: Governor-elect who attacked the Terafab tax break replaces Abbott
keyChanges.description: Gina Hinojosa unseated Greg Abbott on Nov. 3 and takes office in January, Fortune reported on Nov. 5. KBTX's local election coverage confirms she is governor-elect. Abbott's office put Terafab's first phase above $16.8 billion and about 3,000 jobs in Grimes County, with a $30 million Texas Enterprise Fund grant and JETI school-tax relief. Hinojosa's campaign has already pointed at a $1.66 billion JETI break tied to Terafab and sued for Abbott's communications with Musk. The election does not void signed incentives, and Republicans still hold the Texas Senate. Her pledged moratorium targets data-center approvals, and Terafab is a chip plant, but its power and water load sits in the same fight. Later phases, quoted at $55 billion to $119 billion, now depend on a governor who ran against the secrecy of the package. Grimes County tax-abatement records are still sealed.

positive_signals: Signed JETI relief and the enterprise-fund grant are not automatically cancelled
The Texas Senate remains Republican, so repeal is not a one-office act
A data-center freeze does not by itself stop a chip factory
negative_signals: The governor who championed the Grimes County package is out in January
The governor-elect already sued to unseal Abbott-Musk records and campaigned on a $1.66 billion Terafab JETI break
She has pledged to freeze data-center approvals until the Legislature writes new rules, and a 100-million-square-foot fab will face the same power and water scrutiny
Tax-abatement records remain sealed, with no new ruling in the citizens' suit filed last week
Incentive and environmental review can slow phases that are not yet built

key_metrics.actual: Phase one still above $16.8 billion plus a $30 million enterprise grant; JETI not revoked
key_metrics.target: Up to four phases, $55 billion to $119 billion, if every phase is built
key_metrics.trajectory: Political sponsor removed; the abatement itself is unchanged this week

keyChanges.title: Baron floats a $1 trillion Terafab bill; Musk will not fund it now
keyChanges.description: At the Baron Investment Conference on Nov. 6, Ron Baron said Terafab is going to cost a trillion dollars. Musk did not adopt that number. In the Tesla North transcript he answered that the money is not needed immediately and that the project will be built in phases, then pivoted to process experiments. 24/7 Wall St. wrote that he accepted the figure over time; that gloss is stronger than the published transcript, which the outlet itself flags as unchecked against the video. The only official price tag is still the more-than-$16.8 billion first phase at Gibbons Creek. Musk again described an Austin research fab at Giga Texas that will try approaches, many of which will fail, and a production site in Grimes County near Texas A&M. Cutting a year-long cycle to a month is something he thinks the research line may do, not a result. He did not say the Austin building can make a chip, and he did not pull the late-2028 production hope forward. A one-terawatt goal, about 30 times his estimate of 2027 global AI-chip output, remains a target, not capacity.

positive_signals: Musk restated a two-site plan: process trials at Giga Texas, production later in Grimes County
He said the full bill is not due now and that spending would be phased
He still said the plan should succeed at least to some degree
negative_signals: Baron's trillion-dollar figure is not a funded budget, and Musk did not commit it
The state figure for phase one is still just over $16.8 billion
The Austin site is still a process experiment, not a line shipping chips
A year-to-a-month cycle is an untested hope
Headlines that Musk 'said $1 trillion' overread a transcript in which he ducked the number

key_metrics.actual: No chips; official first phase still above $16.8 billion
key_metrics.target: Baron's unfunded $1 trillion versus a one-terawatt output goal
key_metrics.trajectory: The talking point got larger; commissioning and volume dates did not move

keyChanges.title: New FSD seats are temp safety drivers and local supervisors
keyChanges.description: Tesla posted AI Vehicle Operator, Self-Driving - Birmingham on 4 Nov 2026. Euro Top Tech dates the listing that day and links Tesla careers job 288950; RobotTraining's 7 Nov copy of the posting calls it a one-year temporary SI safety operator who drives a prototype 6–8 hours a day on FSD (Supervised) and manual routes, with a weekend day and a license plus five years' history. The posting states no pay. A second Dublin copy of that same temporary role showed as posted about 5 Nov, next to a Dublin listing already up for about two weeks, so Ireland is not new this week. Neither city was in the April 2026 nine-country operator wave (Korea, Hong Kong, Thailand, India, Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Austria, Lithuania, Romania). The same days Tesla added Data Collection Supervisor, Self-Driving seats in secondary US cities: Norfolk about 5 Nov at $73,600–$110,400, plus Knoxville and Corpus Christi about 5 Nov and El Paso about 3 Nov, on top of a 1 Nov cluster (Louisville, Glen Allen, Columbus, Tucson, Cincinnati, Oklahoma City). The supervisor JD is managing hourly vehicle operators, ride-alongs, and personally collecting data. A night-shift Robotaxi Fleet Support supervisor in Peabody, Massachusetts, about 5 Nov at $92,205–$138,308, is one of 22 copies of a cleaning, charging and volunteer-supervision role, including metros with no robotaxi service. That is not a Boston launch.

positive_signals: Birmingham is a UK city that was not in the April 2026 nine-country FSD operator list, and the listing is dated 4 Nov 2026.
Where Tesla states pay, the new Norfolk supervisor band is $73,600–$110,400 and the Peabody fleet-support supervisor band is $92,205–$138,308.
negative_signals: Birmingham is a one-year temporary safety driver still in the seat of an FSD (Supervised) prototype, not an engineering hire and not an unsupervised service.
Dublin already had the same temporary operator role for about two weeks; the 5 Nov listing is a second req, not a new country.
The supervisor wave is ride-alongs and hourly driver management in cities that are not robotaxi markets, including Knoxville, Corpus Christi, Norfolk and El Paso.
The Peabody fleet-support JD supervises volunteers for cleaning and charging and is duplicated across 22 locations, so it is not evidence Tesla opened Boston robotaxi service.

keyChanges.title: AltIndex job-posting counter is not a real hiring collapse
keyChanges.description: AltIndex's Tesla job-posts page, fetched 7 Nov 2026, showed a live estimate of 2,393 active postings and an unlabeled +10.2% badge. That is not comparable to the 8,185 live count filed on 10 Oct, or to the 8,155 still on the series on 29 Oct before it printed 462 and 710. The same page's monthly table still lists October 2026 at 7,445 (−6.1% versus September's 7,928) and August at 5,026, while the FAQ says postings are up 139.3% over the past three months, which would imply a base near 1,000 rather than 5,026. The page also says postings are trending down in the last couple of months. Those statements cannot all be true. A LinkedIn jobs landing snippet still says 7,000+ Tesla jobs in the United States, a rounded marketing floor rather than a census, and it does not corroborate a drop to 2,393. No company-wide total is filed this week. Tesla's own careers search could not be counted: the site returned Akamai 403.

positive_signals: October's AltIndex monthly figure is still 7,445, in the same band as the 8,185 count filed on 10 Oct.
A LinkedIn US jobs landing snippet still says 7,000+, which does not support a collapse to 2,393.
negative_signals: The live counter printed 2,393 on 7 Nov after the series had already shown 462 and 710 following 8,155 on 29 Oct.
The same page claims +139.3% over three months, an October level of 7,445, and a downtrend, which do not reconcile with each other or with August's 5,026.
The +10.2% badge is unlabeled, so it is not a confirmed day-over-day change.

key_metrics.actual: 2,393 live AltIndex count on 2026-11-07, internally inconsistent
key_metrics.trajectory: Series broken; do not treat 2,393 as a hiring freeze

keyChanges.title: Littleton Optimus opening is another data-collection shift lead
keyChanges.description: On 7 Nov 2026 RobotTraining.jobs, which reads Tesla's careers board, listed Data Collection Operations Lead, Optimus in Littleton, Colorado as posted that day. Search indexes point at Tesla requisition 277920 for that city; Tesla.com itself returned Akamai 403, so the body is from RobotTraining's same-day copy. The posting is a Robotics Data Collection Shift Lead, 8:00 a.m.–4:30 p.m. Sunday–Thursday, overseeing collectors. Littleton states no pay. The same title in Fremont lists $25.25–$48.30/hr and was already up about a week, with San Antonio, Tempe, Doral, Marina del Rey, Orlando and Dallas up about three weeks. This follows last week's Littleton data-collection operator listing, already flagged closed. The Optimus data-collection family on that board was 31 postings in 15 places (operators, leads, supervisors), not a new manufacturing-engineer req. The wider robot-training slice the site tracks — safety operators, fleet support and demonstration collection, not Tesla's engineering org — was 178 roles on 6 Nov, unchanged from the week ending 1 Nov, and 175 on 7 Nov. From 10 Oct to 6 Nov that slice added 46 listings and removed 37.

positive_signals: Tesla's board still showed a live Optimus requisition in Littleton on 7 Nov, and the Fremont copy of the same lead states $25.25–$48.30/hr.
The tracked robot-training slice did not collapse this week: 178 open on 6 Nov, the same as the week ending 1 Nov, and 175 on 7 Nov.
negative_signals: The new Littleton seat is an hourly data-collection shift lead, not a manufacturing or AI engineering hire, and it does not state pay.
The same lead title was already open in other cities for one to three weeks, so this is another location, not a new program.
Last week's Littleton operator listing was already flagged closed; visible Optimus hiring remains collectors and shift leads.
On the tracked slice, 10 Oct–6 Nov was replacement churn (+46 new, −37 removed), not a ramp.

keyChanges.title: Canada Model 3 Premium is listed again, but buyers still cannot order it
keyChanges.description: On October 31 Tesla put the Model 3 Premium Rear-Wheel Drive back on the Canadian design page at $39,490 CAD, and Premium All-Wheel Drive at $49,990 CAD. Neither trim has an order button. The page offers Get Updates only. Performance, at $54,990 CAD, is the only Model 3 Canadians can order new. Premium ordering stopped in mid-October after Tesla said demand had used up its quota of China-built EV imports. Tesla has not given a date for reopening those orders. Relisting a price is not a sales restart, and the China import quota is still the constraint.

positive_signals: Premium Rear-Wheel Drive is visible again at $39,490 CAD and Premium All-Wheel Drive at $49,990 CAD
negative_signals: There is no order button, only a Get Updates signup
Performance at $54,990 CAD is the only Model 3 Canadians can order
Tesla has not said when Premium orders reopen after the China-built import quota was used up

keyChanges.title: China keeps November incentives, doubles the Model 3 cut, and discounts used cars
keyChanges.description: On November 1 Tesla China's promotions page took ¥5,000 (about $700) off certified used Model S, 3, X, and Y if the car is ordered and delivered by November 30. New-car offers running October 30 through November 30 moved in opposite directions: the Model 3 final-payment cut rose to ¥10,000 from ¥5,000, while the Model Y cut fell to ¥4,000 from ¥7,000. Paint credits of up to ¥8,000 and 0% financing for up to five years with a ¥39,900 down payment remain. Certified used cars had been excluded from the new-car offers. A smaller Model Y incentive is a modest sign Tesla is not deepening the discount on the main seller. Doubling the Model 3 cut and putting a November 30 delivery deadline on used inventory, in the same week Shanghai posted its weakest wholesale month since February, shows Q4 demand is still being bought. Used-car discounts do not add to new wholesale.

positive_signals: The Model Y final-payment cut was reduced to ¥4,000 from ¥7,000
0% financing for up to five years is still on offer
negative_signals: The Model 3 cash cut was doubled to ¥10,000
A new ¥5,000 certified-used discount requires delivery by November 30, a clearance deadline
Incentives are still in place as Shanghai wholesale just hit its low since February

key_metrics.trajectory: Still discounting into a soft Q4 open

keyChanges.title: Norway keeps Tesla as 2026's top brand while year-to-date volume is down
keyChanges.description: OFV figures cited by TeslaNorth put Tesla first among Norway car brands through October, with 21,523 registrations and a 16.4% share. October was 1,548 cars, a 9.84% share, 55 ahead of Toyota, and the outlet called it Tesla's best October. Model Y accounted for 1,429 of the month and leads 2026 with 17,647 units. Year-to-date Tesla volume is still 3.9% below the same stretch of 2025. Toyota is second at 14,126, up 79.7%, and Volkswagen third at 12,096. Chinese brands took a record 22.5% of October registrations. First place in a small, already electric market, with the year's volume still down, is not a global delivery rebound.

positive_signals: October registrations of 1,548 beat Toyota by 55 and were described as Tesla's best October
Year-to-date lead of 21,523 and a 16.4% share, with Model Y at 17,647
negative_signals: Year-to-date volume is still 3.9% below 2025
October's 1,548 units are a small absolute contribution
Chinese brands' October share hit a record 22.5%

key_metrics.trajectory: Brand lead held, units still down year over year

keyChanges.title: Shanghai October wholesale falls to 67,829, lowest month since February
keyChanges.description: CPCA preliminary data released November 3 put Giga Shanghai wholesale at 67,829 vehicles in October, up 10.30% year over year and down 28.88% from September's 95,366. That is the lowest month since February's 58,599 and the second-lowest of 2026. Year-to-date wholesale is 810,889, up 21.42%, slower than the 22.54% pace through September. The flash print does not split domestic sales and exports. Through September, domestic deliveries were 381,088, down 11.93%, while exports of 361,972 were up 108.44% and were 48.71% of wholesale. China's passenger NEV wholesale estimate for October was 1.80 million, up 12% year over year and 8% from September, so Tesla lagged the market on both comparisons. TeslaNorth, citing the same flash report, ranked Tesla eighth among NEV makers, with BYD at 483,125. Ten straight year-over-year monthly gains do not make a Q4 rebound. The quarter opened at a low, domestic demand was already falling, and October's export mix is still unpublished.

positive_signals: October wholesale rose 10.30% year over year, the tenth straight monthly year-over-year gain
Year-to-date Shanghai wholesale of 810,889 is up 21.42%
negative_signals: Down 28.88% from September to 67,829, the low since February and the second-lowest month of 2026
No domestic-versus-export split; through September domestic deliveries were already down 11.93% while exports carried the wholesale total
Tesla lagged a passenger NEV market that rose 8% month over month and 12% year over year
CPCA labels the figures preliminary and says they can differ from later final prints

key_metrics.trajectory: Q4 opened well below the September peak

keyChanges.title: Germany October registrations quadruple year over year but trail BYD
keyChanges.description: Germany's KBA said on November 4 that Tesla registered 2,932 vehicles in October, up 290.9% year over year. January through October is 47,742, up 206.1%, a 1.9% year-to-date share. October share was 1.2% of 254,492 cars. BYD registered 5,173 (2.0% share) and Leapmotor 3,661 (1.4%). BYD's year-to-date total is 47,961, 219 units ahead of Tesla. Battery-electric cars were 94,086, up 79.5%, a 37.0% share. The year-over-year jump is off a weak October 2025 base. Teslarati's recap of the prior KBA month put September at 12,552, so October is roughly a 77% sequential drop after the quarter-end spike. The recovery versus 2025 is real. October is not a sustained run rate, and Tesla is not the volume leader for the month or the year to date.

positive_signals: October registrations of 2,932 were up 290.9% year over year
Year-to-date registrations of 47,742 were up 206.1%
German BEV registrations rose 79.5% to a 37.0% share
negative_signals: October share was only 1.2%, and both BYD and Leapmotor outsold Tesla in the month
BYD leads year to date, 47,961 to 47,742

The year-over-year percentage is an easy comparison with a depressed October 2025

keyChanges.title: Korea import lead hits nine months, but October volume fell 26%
keyChanges.description: Tesla Korea said on November 6 that it was South Korea's top imported-car brand for a ninth straight month, February through October, citing KAIDA. TeslaNorth, citing The Korea Times and Businesskorea on that KAIDA file, reported 9,165 October registrations, more than double the 4,350 of a year earlier, but down 25.9% from September. KAIDA attributed the sequential drop to supply shortages. Model Y Premium led imported models, ahead of the Mercedes-Benz E 200 and the Model 3. January-October registrations were 98,313. Imported passenger cars overall were 31,117, up 29.3% year over year. The new post does not repeat a claim that Model Y was the best-selling car in the whole Korean market in October. An import-brand streak excludes Hyundai and Kia as domestic brands, and the month itself was down.

Ninth straight month as the leading import brand, with year-to-date registrations of 98,313
negative_signals: October volume fell 25.9% from September
KAIDA pointed to supply shortages, so the drop is not framed as clean demand
The ranking is imports only and does not include domestic Hyundai and Kia
Tesla did not repeat an overall-market best-seller claim for October

key_metrics.trajectory: Up year over year, down month over month

keyChanges.title: Musk sets Cybertruck wind-down for mid-2027 after another US price hike
keyChanges.description: On November 6 Elon Musk wrote that Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production at Gigafactory Texas around the middle of 2027 to free floor space for more Cybercab output. He gave no hard stop, no residual truck rate, no plan for existing orders, and no Cybercab build number. Lead engineer Wes Morrill said spare parts and service will continue. The day before, the US design page raised cash prices again: Premium All-Wheel Drive to $92,490, up $7,500 from the $84,990 August sticker and about 16% above the roughly $79,990 level early in 2026; Cyberbeast to $102,490; Dual Motor listed at $82,490 but grayed out for new orders. Tesla posted no product note. Australia and New Zealand Cybertruck plans were already cancelled in October. This is an exit from an underperforming pickup, not a disclosed robotaxi production rate.

positive_signals: Morrill said spare parts and service support continue for trucks already on the road
The wind-down is aimed at mid-2027, so some Cybertruck output can continue into the first half of next year
negative_signals: No residual rate, no alternate factory, and no replacement pickup
No Cybercab unit figure attached to the freed lines
Premium sticker is $92,490 after another hike, and the cheaper Dual Motor trim is not selectable for new orders
Tesla's own accounts had not followed Musk's post with a product note

key_metrics.trajectory: Line exit, not a volume ramp

keyChanges.title: Tesla sets Argentina launch for November 20 with no prices or orders
keyChanges.description: Tesla and Tesla Latinoamérica set an Argentina debut for November 20, and the main Tesla account reposted the date. Cencosud had already said the first store will be a Level 1 space at Unicenter in Martínez, with two vehicles on display and a ten-car test-drive zone in a parking lot, not a traditional dealer. Tesla has not published prices, an order page, a Find Us pin, or which models go on sale. The regional video shows a Model Y. Talk of a 2027 sales ramp and extra Buenos Aires sites is outside both Tesla's posts and Cencosud's release. A dated greeting plus a two-car mall showroom is a market entry on the calendar. It does not add 2026 deliveries.

The stop follows earlier South America retail steps in Chile and Colombia
negative_signals: No prices, no configurator, and no named launch models
The confirmed retail format is two display cars and a ten-car test-drive zone
A 2027 volume ramp is not in Tesla's or Cencosud's statements
